cases.note: The loop iterates units from largest to smallest and breaks on the first threshold met, exactly matching the original if/else chain, with 'B' as fallback. This is an equivalent refactor with no observable behaviour change.

The explicit integer pattern for the core int tag was changed from '[-+]?0b[0-1]+' to '[^-+]?0b[0-1]+', so explicitly tagged negative (or positive) binary literals like '!!int "-0b101"' no longer resolve and now throw a YAMLException instead of returning -5.

cases.note: The change is a pure refactor of parseYamlInteger$2: it renames the local variable and hoists the digits.slice(2) computation, which was already performed identically in each branch. All arithmetic and parsing behaviour is unchanged.

The type check was replaced with a constant `true`, so any non-string value with a truthy length (e.g. an array like ['2 days']) is passed to parse instead of throwing. The original code threw an Error for such inputs.
